cards.title: llama.cpp Releases v1.0.0 with Semantic Versioning and Stable API Commitment
cards.why_it_matters: If you build or depend on local inference tooling, llama.cpp hitting v1.0.0 means API/ABI stability guarantees are now formalized — a meaningful signal for production pipeline planning.
cards.summary: llama.cpp v1.0.0 formalizes semantic versioning for llama.cpp and ggml, with major-version bumps reserved for API/ABI breaking changes. The release supports 150+ model architecture variants, all mainstream speculative decoding methods, and hardware backends from NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM, and Intel loaded as dynamic libraries. CI infrastructure scales via Hugging Face Buckets and Jobs with self-hosted runners across major platforms.

cards.title: Google DeepMind Open-Sources SatWeave and PARDIG Datasets Behind WeatherNext 3 AI Weather Model
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers working on foundation models for physical systems or climate/Earth observation applications, these are production-quality, globally-covering datasets with live feeds — a rare open release from a leading lab.
cards.summary: DeepMind is releasing SatWeave, an hourly global mosaic of geostationary satellite imagery from five satellites (GOES-East/West, Meteosat 0, Meteosat Indian Ocean, Himawari), and PARDIG, a 15-minute-resolution global precipitation dataset at ~10 km resolution trained on NASA GPM sparse radar observations using SatWeave and ECMWF fields as inputs. PARDIG outperforms NASA's IMERG-Final across all analyzed rain rates, improving hourly precipitation detection skill by more than 30% on light-to-moderate precipitation. Historical archives and live feeds are both available.

cards.title: XYBench: 8K-Question Benchmark Tests Whether LLMs Redirect Misguided User Requests
cards.why_it_matters: Knowing that Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-9B, and DeepSeek-V4 Pro all systematically fail to redirect users away from mistaken approaches is directly relevant to evaluating and improving assistant-style models you may build or deploy.
cards.summary: XYBench (Best Resource Paper, EMNLP 2026) contains 8,115 real-world questions from Stack Overflow, Stack Exchange, WikiHow, and manual curation, each annotated with a stated request (Y) and underlying goal (X). Five evaluated frontier models — Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-9B, DeepSeek-V4 Pro — consistently addressed Y while failing to steer users toward X, unlike human reference answers. Developed with CMU, NVIDIA, and Johns Hopkins.

cards.title: Controlled Study Finds Dedicated Vision Capacity — Not Pretrained Encoders — Is What Multimodal LLMs Actually Need
cards.why_it_matters: This controlled ablation directly informs architectural decisions for anyone designing or fine-tuning multimodal models, clarifying which of three commonly conflated design choices actually drives visual understanding performance.
cards.summary: Pretraining all models from scratch on common data at matched compute, researchers disentangle three bundled choices in multimodal vision encoding: visual prior, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement. Key findings: a visual prior (pretrained encoder) is not necessary — joint training from scratch matches it. Dedicated vision capacity is necessary — encoder-free models underperform even when backbone size is increased to compensate. Pre-fusion placement is not necessary — in-fusion early-layer vision modules match encoder performance and reduce time to first token.

cards.title: ArchSpace: Public Platform for Recording and Peer-Reviewing LLM Architecture Research with Scaling-Law Validation
cards.why_it_matters: As a research engineer tracking architectural innovations from labs like DeepSeek and Qwen, ArchSpace offers a structured venue to evaluate whether small-scale architecture experiments extrapolate — before committing to expensive large-scale runs.
cards.summary: ArchSpace is a public platform for documenting LLM architecture proposals with their experiments and reasoning, community review, and citation tracking. It uses scaling laws to predict model loss at larger scales from small experiments, addressing the gap where industry teams rarely publish what failed and academia lacks consistent baselines. Initial references include Qwen3.5 and OLMo3 baselines with fitted scaling laws and a reusable training recipe.

cards.title: AgentSSL: MLE Agents Can Synthesize Semi-Supervised Learning Pipelines, Beating Human Baselines in 8 of 12 Settings
cards.why_it_matters: This extends the emerging MLE-agent paradigm into the semi-supervised regime — a realistic and underexplored setting — with concrete benchmark results and an identified bottleneck (program selection) that points to open research problems.
cards.summary: AgentSSL frames semi-supervised learning as a program search problem and evaluates MLE agents under limited labeled data. Agents exceeded the strongest human-engineered SSL baselines in 8 of 12 settings by up to +21.8%. However, program selection is a critical bottleneck: choosing programs based on the agent's own feedback metric degrades performance by up to 47%. The paper introduces ProgramSelectBench with 16,977 agent-generated and human-engineered SSL programs to study selection methods, and validates on real-world ecology detection tasks.

cards.title: Nvidia Isaac Sim Gets 'SimReady' Open Asset Library on Hugging Face for Robot Simulation
cards.why_it_matters: If you work on robotics ML pipelines, SimReady Central gives you validated, plug-and-play OpenUSD assets with collision, mass, and joint metadata — cutting the painful setup that precedes any sim-to-real work.
cards.summary: SimReady Central, an open Hugging Face library, provides OpenUSD robot and object assets pre-validated against simulation profiles covering joints, drives, collisions, and mass. A walkthrough uses the UR17G arm, Robotiq 2F-140 gripper, and a beverage can in Isaac Sim 6.2, with agent-generated task code (demonstrated with GPT-6 Sol) to execute pick-and-place. Assets include models and simulation settings; users add scene assembly and task control logic.

cards.title: Neurosymbolic RL Reduces Portfolio Mandate Violations from ~97% to 4.8% in Continuous Action Space
cards.why_it_matters: The extension of neurosymbolic constraint satisfaction (PLPG-style) to continuous action spaces is a technically interesting RL result relevant to anyone working on constrained policy learning or safe RL beyond discrete settings.
cards.summary: The paper extends Probabilistic Logic Policy Gradient (PLPG) to continuous portfolio allocation, using reparameterized Monte Carlo sampling to estimate the probability that the policy's executed action satisfies a six-rule, regime-conditional investment mandate, adding this estimate to the training objective. Without post-hoc correction at inference, the method reduces mandate violations from 96–98% (unconstrained RL) and 33.4% (reward-penalty baseline) to 4.8%, demonstrating that continuous-action policies can internalize symbolic constraints.
